title: Thyroid storm
stem: Resus 1. A 20-year-old woman is brought in confused and agitated. BP 200/105, HR 142 (irregular), SpO2 97%, temperature 40.2 °C. Her mother says she has been taking 'slimming pills' bought online.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on; examine her yourself: what is the differential?

phases.title: Cool and settle
phases.goal: Cool her and settle the agitation safely.

phases.title: Treat the storm
phases.goal: Beta-blocker, thionamide, steroid — then iodine an hour after the PTU.

events.say: It is an hour since the PTU.

review.text: Doses. Your notes give PTU 250 mg every 4–6 hours with no loading dose, and hydrocortisone 200 mg then 100 mg every 6–8 hours. The ATA gives a PTU load of 500–1000 mg then 250 mg every 4 hours, and hydrocortisone 300 mg IV then 100 mg every 8 hours. Propranolol is 60–80 mg every 4 hours rather than 80–120 mg every 6 hours.

notes:
Checked against the American Thyroid Association 2016 guidelines on hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis, the Japan Thyroid Association 2016 criteria, and the Burch–Wartofsky Point Scale (1993).

Differential for fever, agitation and tachycardia: sepsis/meningitis, thyroid storm, sympathomimetic or serotonergic toxicity, anticholinergic toxicity, heat stroke, NMS. A goitre and the history point to storm; the Burch–Wartofsky score (45 or more highly suggestive) supports it.

Treatment (ATA): beta-blocker (propranolol 60–80 mg orally every 4 hours, or IV/esmolol if unable; caution in heart failure); thionamide — PTU 500–1000 mg load then 250 mg every 4 hours (preferred in storm because it also blocks T4→T3 conversion) or methimazole 60–80 mg/day; iodine (potassium iodide or Lugol's) at least 1 hour after the thionamide; hydrocortisone 300 mg IV load then 100 mg every 8 hours; supportive care: cooling, paracetamol (avoid aspirin — displaces thyroxine), fluids, treat the trigger, ICU. Cholestyramine for exogenous hormone (e.g. slimming products containing thyroid hormone or tiratricol).

Your notes: PTU 250 mg every 4–6 hours (no loading dose), hydrocortisone 200 mg then 100 mg every 6–8 hours, propranolol 80–120 mg every 6 hours; ATA uses a PTU load of 500–1000 mg and hydrocortisone 300 mg load. The order (thionamide, then iodine an hour later), the differential, and CHP reporting of illegal slimming drugs match.

Perfect script checked against the ATA 2016 guideline, a toxicology differential checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (tenfold doses, aspirin, PTU without a load, low hydrocortisone). Added: the differential and the Burch–Wartofsky score said aloud, cholestyramine, and reporting the product.

Time drives this station: a TIME clock on the HUD. Iodine comes due an hour after the PTU. When everything due is done, the clock runs ahead to the next timed moment instead of making you wait it out.

Toxidrome.mark: Excludes other toxidromes (no clonus, sweating present)

steps.hint: ECG, TFT, glucose, electrolytes, cultures, tox screen, pregnancy test.

Now.r: TSH < 0.01, free T4 > 100 pmol/L. "With fever 40, AF, agitation: Burch–Wartofsky well over 45: thyroid storm."

Now.r: K 3.0, ALT 90, hCG negative, drug screen negative.
Now.mark: Broad screen including pregnancy and toxicology

qs.q: Why give iodine at least 1 hour after PTU?
qs.a: So iodine isn't used to make more hormone
wrong: Iodine inactivates PTU if given at the same time

qs.q: Why PTU rather than carbimazole in storm?
qs.a: It also blocks peripheral T4→T3 conversion
wrong: It has fewer side effects, including liver injury

qs.q: Score used to support thyroid storm?
Public health step for an illegal slimming product?
qs.a: Report to the Department of Health
wrong: Tell the pharmacist who sold it, and no one else

script.say: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2, IV access and a core temperature.
Fever, agitation and tachycardia: the differential is sepsis or meningitis, thyroid storm, a sympathomimetic or serotonergic toxidrome, and heat stroke.
No meningism. A smooth goitre with a bruit; lid retraction and proptosis; a fine tremor, warm sweaty palms. Pupils normal, sweating, bowel sounds present, no clonus: not another toxidrome.
12-lead ECG, thyroid function; glucose, electrolytes, LFTs, cultures, a urine drug screen and a pregnancy test.
script.do: Fast AF at 140; TSH under 0.01, free T4 over 100; K 3.0.

script.say: Fever 40, fast AF, agitation and thyrotoxic: a Burch–Wartofsky score well over 45: this is thyroid storm.
Active cooling: blanket, fans, tepid sponging. Diazepam 5 to 10 mg IV, titrated. Paracetamol 1 g IV; no aspirin, it frees more thyroid hormone.
Propranolol 60 to 80 mg every 4 hours. PTU with a loading dose, 500 to 1000 mg, then 250 mg every 4 hours. Hydrocortisone 300 mg IV, then 100 mg every 8 hours.
Iodine an hour after the PTU: Lugol's, 5 drops every 6 hours.
IV fluids, correct the potassium of 3.0, and ICU referral. If it's exogenous hormone from the pills: cholestyramine to bind it.
